notes: The fix: the special `w[-1]+w[::-1]` rule is not "applied to the last token" but "applied to the token that ends at the end of the string." When the input has trailing whitespace (`"a b "`, `" x "`), no token qualifies, so every token gets plain reversal — which is why E6's `"ab c"` gives `"ba cc"` (first token plain-reversed) while `"c ab"` gives `"c bba"` (last token, ending at string end, gets
